live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating oshb:Ezek.1.1-1.3 as its own superscription unit, separate from the vision it introduces. Rejected because the vision proper (1:4-1:28) carries no independent onset device of its own - it simply continues the sentence the hand-of-YHWH clause opens - so cutting after 1:3 would manufacture a seam the bytes do not mark, and would still leave a 25-verse remainder with the same cap problem.
live_prose.device_notes: Whole-chapter span (28 verses), well above the 7-10 typical density and above the 14-16 stretch cap for measured/listed blocks even though this is not such a block; disclosed and held at low confidence rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut. MT 1:3 is cited only under the 49-verse any-form word-event count, never blended with the 48-verse first-person family. K/Q at 1:8 checked before quoting: the unit does not splice the disputed word. The OSHB editorial note at 1:11 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus, not a reading change. Paseq at 1:1 and 1:27 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position is claimed.

A pe is recorded after this verse; the inventory does not carry intra-verse position, so no claim is made about whether the mark falls before or after 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) (“I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.3.17)). live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) (“Yahweh’s hand was there on me” (web:Ezek.3.22)), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, where the construct accompanies the spirit carrying the prophet away, a transit rather than a new scene) because it opens a fresh scene: “Arise, go out into the plain” (web:Ezek.3.22). 3:25 announces that עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') will be put on the prophet; the word recurs at 4:8 in the siege sign-act, across the 3:27/4:1 seam (accent_stripped tier: the same consonants and vowels under a different accent), so the muteness command and the sign-acts share a device, and that continuity is weighed here against the seam even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) (“He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house” (web:Ezek.3.27)) - the sixth verse in chapters 2-3 to name the rebellious house (sweep: 12 verses book-wide name it, six of them in chapters 2-3), and the parent P1's close; a samekh is recorded after this verse. Across the seam, 4:1 opens with וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('and you, son of man'), spliced at byte tier as the 3:27 clause is, and turns to the command to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-acts. The unit therefore stops at 3:27 and does not extend into 4:1; the seam's near side is closed by the refrain and the samekh after 3:27 (single witness), and its far side is opened by that sub-onset.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Placing the P1/P2 parent seam at 3:15/3:16 instead of 3:27/4:1, on the strength of 3:16's own strict word-event and the seven-day close it answers. Weighed on the bytes, the onset side of that seam is strong: 3:16 sets מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16)) before its strict word-event, and a pe follows 3:16 itself (single witness), after the word-event verse rather than before it. Its close side is narrative: 3:15 ends the journey to the exiles on seven days of sitting among them, a report rather than a refrain. The rebellious-house refrain runs on both sides of 3:16 (sweep: of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, four stand before 3:16 and two after it), so a parent seam there would divide that series, whereas at 3:27/4:1 the series' sixth verse stands on the close side and the sub-onset of 4:1 on the onset side. The alternative is kept as a held question and not argued away, because the ropes of 3:25, taken up at 4:8, tie the muteness command (3:22-27) to the sign-acts (4:1-17) across the later seam.

live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that opens P2 (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam at oshb:Ezek.3.27. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) recurs the exact word from 3:25 on the far side of the parent seam, disclosed as continuity evidence already weighed at that seam. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe recorded after it, before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. How the sign-acts of chs 4-7 divide is an open question, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. The mark on the verse before this cut is weighed as corroboration for the alternative: on the rival's far face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3 (single-witness), and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the rival's near face the candidate onset oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, no verse of ch 4 belongs to the counted messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event formula classes, the chapter's only counted device verses being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is neither an utterance-formula verse (sweep: 81 verses) nor a member of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses) - and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side. A ve'attah inside an open unit begins a sub-unit only when the addressee changes or the verse before it ends on a verse-final close-role formula; neither holds here, and a mark by itself never supplies that close. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. The address forms bear this out, 4:3 included, the very verse the mark follows: the titled sub-onset וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ stands at 4:1 and again at 5:1, whereas bare וְאַתָּ֤ה without the title opens three interior stages - 4:3, 4:4 and 4:9 - so the text stages the siege-model, the iron pan, the two lying postures and the rationed food as one commanded act and not as separate commands (oshb:Ezek.4.1).

Two K/Q verses checked before quoting (4:6, 4:15); 4:6 also carries an editorial note tied to the same disputed consonant, disclosed together. Paseq at 4:9 disclosed count-only, single-witness. MT 3:27 is followed by a samekh (single witness); the sign-act series that opens at 4:1 has this mark standing immediately before it. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 4:12 (single witness); the unit does not cut there because the food-rationing act begun at 4:9 continues without a fresh 'son of man' address or messenger formula reopening the speech. A further samekh stands after MT 4:14 (single witness) inside the span; no cut is made there either, since 4:15's concession is Yahweh's reply within the same rationing scene, not a fresh address.

live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: 5:1 וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם קַח לְךָ֣ חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.5.1) (“You, son of man, take a sharp sword” (web:Ezek.5.1)), a fresh 'son of man' sub-onset distinct from 4:1's - a new symbolic object (sword/razor/hair) rather than a continuation of the siege-tile act. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues “Moreover I will make you a desolation” (web:Ezek.5.14) with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). The verdict is bound to the sign-act itself by a byte-identical clause: 5:12 closes with the same words that close 5:2, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.5.2; oshb:Ezek.5.12) ('and I will draw a sword after them', sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the third at 12:14).
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 5:13 or 5:15, the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, also weighed here, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, which would set the sign-act 5:1-4 against the interpretation 5:5-17. Its far face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 (single witness) and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it is neither an utterance-formula verse nor one of the verses of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its near face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But a messenger formula counts as a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither condition holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet the second condition by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.
live_prose.device_notes: 17-verse unit, one verse past the 14-16 stretch cap; disclosed rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. Three of those five marks coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them.
